NOON REPORT - MV TORMAR SPRING
Date/time: 26 Jan 2025 1200 (ship's time UTC)
Position: 50-50.2N 031-32.2W
Distance run last 24h: 231.3 nm
Average speed last 24h: 12.5 kn
ROB VLSFO: 1019.0 t
ROB MGO: 94.5 t
Consumption last 24h: VLSFO 18.8 t, MGO 0.1 t
Next port: Sept-Iles
ETA Sept-Iles: 2025-01-31 1100 UTC
ETA based on: 12.5 kn
Remarks: Main engine stopped 0610-1140 UTC: low lube oil pressure alarm. Cause traced to a blocked strainer; strainer cleaned, pressure normal, engine restarted and passage resumed. Average speed over 18.5 h steaming. Fuel used during stoppage: VLSFO 1.1 t (generators and boiler).

Master MV TORMAR SPRING

summary: Voyage Agent reports: The Master's ETA is consistent. No ETA notice is due at this time.

result.result:
The Master's ETA is consistent. No ETA notice is due at this time.

The main engine stop from 06:10 to 11:40 UTC on 26 Jan 2025 is consistent with the report. According to the off-hire clause, time lost through a breakdown of machinery (blocked strainer) is off hire. Based on simulated figures, the off-hire period of 5.5 hours would result in a hire deduction of 2,177.08 USD and bunker costs of 660.00 USD (1.1 t VLSFO), totaling 2,837.08 USD to the owner's account. The operator should decide whether to put the ship off hire for this period and notify the owner. If approved, this would involve: (a) a voyage management system entry for the off-hire period, and (b) an e-mail to the owner's vessel technical management providing the period and reason and requesting the engine log extract for the stop.
